display.purpose: Hero panel page title. One per page.

headline.purpose: ui_section titles — the label on a grouped region. Drops to 0.9rem below lg.

title.purpose: Table column headings, card section headings, form legends.

body.purpose: All prose and table data. Tight 1.2 leading is what makes long tables scannable.

label.purpose: The data-label prefix in front of each value when a table folds into cards below 1024px.

shadows.name: region-lift
shadows.purpose: The .box container and .me-hero-panel only. Wide, diffuse, directionless — a sheet of paper on a desk, not an elevated widget.

shadows.name: surface-hint
shadows.purpose: Cards and table containers. Separates a surface from the page without raising it.

motion.name: drill-slide
motion.purpose: Sidebar drill-down panes sliding horizontally between levels. Disabled under prefers-reduced-motion.

motion.name: copy-success
motion.purpose: Overshooting ease for the clipboard-copy confirmation — the icon zooms and fades upward over 500ms while the button flashes success green over 1s.

motion.name: chevron-rotate
motion.purpose: Detail-row toggle chevron flips when aria-expanded becomes true, so a reader can see which rows they have already opened.

breakpoints.name: md
breakpoints.purpose: Where a phone stops being a phone. Below it .button-row stacks every control onto its own line; from here up the row wraps instead. Not a layout fold — the table fold and the sidebar drawer both still run to lg.

breakpoints.name: lg
breakpoints.purpose: The structural breakpoint. Tables fold to cards, the sidebar drawer overlays, sticky button rows go static. Must be expressed as (width < theme(--breakpoint-lg)), never max-width — both bounds are inclusive and a max-width fold matches at exactly 1024px at the same time as lg:.

breakpoints.name: hq-shared-display
breakpoints.purpose: HQ only. Above it the HQ shell and its sidebar take zoom: 1.15 (1.35 above 2400px) and the content column caps at 64rem with prose at 68ch, so a screen read from across the room spends its width on legibility instead of line length. Screen only; print must never inherit it. See components/hq-window.css.

touchFloor.purpose: Minimum size for anything interactive. btn-sm and select-sm are explicitly bumped from DaisyUI's 32px to 9 size steps to clear it.

narrative.overview:
Clubhouse 3 looks like a reference document engineered to be read fast under bad conditions. Every decision in the system trades ornament for the ability to find one fact on a crowded page — in dust and glare on a phone, on a shared HQ screen at 3am, or in a nine-hour administrative session across hundreds of rows. The type is hyperlegible by design rather than by taste, the body scale is a tight 0.9rem on a 1.2 line-height, and table cells are padded at 6px. Density here is not crowding; it is the refusal to make someone scroll for something that could have fit.

The surfaces are warm and the ink is cool. In light mode every base surface sits at hue 80 — a faint paper-tan — while the single chromatic voice, a mid-blue primary at hue 262, appears only on things you can act on. In dark mode the surfaces flip cool (hue 260) but the text stays warm (hue 80), so the page reads as ink on stone in both directions rather than as one theme inverted. The result is a document that feels made of material, not of rectangles.

What the system explicitly refuses: decorative color, colored text as emphasis, competing accents, and any component invented ad hoc. Color carries meaning or it does not appear. Emphasis is weight and size. New components and new color styling both require approval before they exist, which is why the visual vocabulary has stayed small across roughly twenty functional namespaces.
keyCharacteristics: One typeface for everything — Atkinson Hyperlegible, proportional, carrying display, headline, title, body and label alike. The monospaced cut of the same design is reserved for code and literal strings.
Warm surfaces in light, cool surfaces in dark, warm text in both.
A single rationed accent; semantic status colors only where status exists.
Flat at rest; a soft diffuse shadow marks a whole grouped region, not a widget.
A 4px start border is the system's signature mark for "this belongs together".
Every table becomes a stack of labeled cards below 1024px.
36px is the floor for anything a finger touches, without exception.

rules.name: The Rationed Accent Rule
rules.body: Signal Blue is the only chromatic color permitted in ordinary chrome. If a screen has more than one non-semantic color competing for the eye, one of them is wrong.

rules.name: The Two-Temperature Rule
rules.body: Light surfaces are warm (hue 80) and dark surfaces are cool (hue 260), while text is warm in both. Never author a surface color that breaks its mode's temperature.

rules.name: The Semantic-Only Rule
rules.body: Raw Tailwind color utilities (text-gray-700, bg-white, dark:bg-gray-800) are banned outright. Use DaisyUI semantic tokens or the bridge tokens (text-body, text-heading, bg-default). This is what keeps both themes correct for free.

rules.name: The Weight-Not-Color Rule
rules.body: Emphasis is font-semibold and a size step, never a color change. Color that does not encode status is noise.

rules.name: The One Typeface Rule
rules.body: There is no second family. Atkinson Hyperlegible is the default for everything; reach for font-mono only when characters have to align in columns or a value is meant to be read as a literal string — a document tag, a client ID, a raw log line. Setting prose, headings, labels, or table text in the mono cut is a bug, not a style. If a design needs a display face to be distinctive, it needs a better idea instead.

rules.name: The Aligned Numbers Rule
rules.body: The proportional cut sets figures at their natural widths, so every table asks for font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums and columns of hours, dates and counts line up without anything being set in the mono face. Outside a table, reach for the tabular-nums utility when digits stack vertically.

rules.name: The Tight Leading Rule
rules.body: Body leading is 1.2, not 1.5. Space between rows is bought with padding where it aids grouping, never spent uniformly as line-height.

rules.name: The 1024 Fold Rule
rules.body: The responsive fold is written as @media (width < theme(--breakpoint-lg)) — the exact negation of Tailwind's lg:. A max-width: 64rem fold overlaps lg: at exactly 1024px, and content carrying hidden lg:table-cell beside an lg:hidden stand-in then belongs to neither layout and renders nowhere. Never express this fold as max-width.

rules.name: The Top-Align Rule
rules.body: Table rows align to the top, set once on :where(tbody) so the specificity stays at zero. When one cell holds a wrapped note and its neighbor holds a single date, middle alignment floats the short cell away from the row's first line and the eye loses which value belongs to which record.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: A new component gets no shadow. Region lift is reserved for containers that group an entire section of a page; anything smaller separates itself with a border or a tonal step.

rules.name: The Left-Bar Rule
rules.body: A 4px start border means "these things are one group". Do not use it for emphasis, for status, or as decoration — its value is that it means exactly one thing.

dos: Do reach for ButtonHelper (button_action, button_link, submit_button, delete_button) and AppFormBuilder / ui_form. Raw <button> and bare form_with are not part of this system.
Do wrap a group of related fields in a fieldset so it inherits the 4px start border and gradient — the chunking is an accessibility feature, not a decoration.
Do hold every interactive element at 36px minimum, including btn-sm, which is explicitly bumped to 9 size steps for this reason.
Do write the responsive fold as @media (width < theme(--breakpoint-lg)).
Do pass striped: false on any table that uses detail rows.
Do name a row's state with t.row state: rather than painting a background at the call site, and make the tinted row say why in words, a badge, or an icon as well.

Do give every user-facing element a dark-mode result, and verify it by toggling both data-theme and the .dark class — the app uses a custom dark variant keyed on the class, so changing only one produces a false reading.
Do state status in words as well as color, since color alone fails both colorblind users and a sunlit phone screen.

Do spend a surface's chroma on what is still owed, not on what is finished. A completed step recedes to muted and keeps its glyph; the step that is next carries the accent, and any live state worth finding at a distance carries the semantic tone it already uses elsewhere on the page. A checklist whose only colored item is the one already done points the eye at the past.
donts: Don't use raw Tailwind color utilities anywhere. text-gray-700, bg-white, and dark:bg-gray-800 are banned; semantic tokens and bridge tokens are the only vocabulary.
Don't introduce a new component or a new color treatment without approval. The vocabulary is small on purpose.
Don't add a shadow to a new component. Flat is the default; region lift belongs to .box and the hero panel.
Don't use color for emphasis. Use font-semibold and a size step.
Don't spend vertical space that carries no grouping meaning. Excess whitespace is a defect in a product where users scan hundreds of rows.
Don't invent a second typeface, and don't set prose, headings, labels or table text in the mono cut — tables align their figures with font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums, not by changing face.

Don't reach past text-body-subtle for a secondary line. It was an alias of text-body and communicated nothing; it is now a real step (oklch(50% 0.012 60) light, oklch(66% 0.012 80) dark) — lightness only, on base-content's own hue, set at the lightest step that still clears 4.5:1 on the base-300 row-hover fill.
Don't extend the sidebar's literal hex palette to new surfaces. It is documented as existing chrome, not as an available color system.
